core.title: Type every flow router message payload
core.given: A flow router in a plan artifact contains messages (newly authored or pre-existing)
core.when: The flow router is taken to CONFIRM
core.then: Every flow router message declares either payload.contract or an explicit payload.no_payload_reason.
prefer: Set payload.contract to the contract that types the data the message carries
When the message carries no data, set payload.no_payload_reason stating why
avoid: Leaving any message (including unchanged, pre-existing ones) with neither payload.contract nor payload.no_payload_reason
Empty or placeholder no_payload_reason used only to satisfy the check while the message actually carries data
core.why: Flow router messages are integration points between participants; an untyped payload leaves the handoff ambiguous, and downstream payload checks (contract body, registry membership) presuppose a typed payload.
evidence: The realization's validator for this rule passes
For each flow router message, payload.contract or payload.no_payload_reason is present
verification: Checked when the plan reaches the CONFIRM phase; enforcement is confirm-blocking: the plan cannot be confirmed while any flow router message lacks both payload.contract and payload.no_payload_reason.
The check evaluates every message of the flow router, including unchanged, pre-existing messages.

The check is a presence check: it verifies only that each message declares payload.contract or payload.no_payload_reason; it does not validate the contract's body or its registry membership (separate rules presuppose this one).
The check's subject is the flow router as a whole (subject kind: flow router), not individual changed files.
A finding reports the offending flow router, the offending message, its payload, and the reason.

fires: CONFIRM is reached for a plan containing a flow router that has at least one message, including messages that were not added or edited in the current change (the check then evaluates each message for payload.contract or payload.no_payload_reason)
doesNotFire: The subject being validated is not a flow router (no flow router subject present)

bunOnly.reason: Names this rule's concrete validator (a Bun validator test id); the core states the same evidence generically as 'the realization's validator for this rule passes'.
The term id payload_typed is an identifier of this rule's realization; the definition it names is the obligation itself, restated neutrally in core.then.
The validation template and variant ids identify this one rule's checker in the Bun realization; the core describes the check generically as a presence check (core.verification).

bunOnly.text: Failure evidence fields: flow_router_id, message_id, payload, reason
bunOnly.reason: Concrete finding-field names of this rule's Bun checker; the core describes the finding content generically (a finding reports the flow router, the message, the payload, the reason).

neutralityNotes: This convention constrains the content of plan artifacts (flow router, message, payload.contract, payload.no_payload_reason) and the planning lifecycle (CONFIRM phase, confirm-blocking). These are ATDD-methodology terms, at the same level as user/system flow / product capability / DESIRED OUTCOME which the closed vocabulary already treats as neutral, so the core names them directly and needs no profile key: no path, suffix, idiom, runtime or tooling construct appears in the rule. Consequently profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The only realization-specific content is this one rule's checker identifiers: the validator test id, the term id payload_typed, the validation template/variant ids, and the concrete finding-field names; all are recorded in bunOnly, while core.verification describes the check generically (presence check at CONFIRM, confirm-blocking, severity 3, strict, subject = flow router, evaluates unchanged messages too, does not check contract body or registry membership). The observer notes attached to the activation facts in bun.json were dropped from the fact objects (the output schema has no note field); their content is preserved by the observability value needs_new_observer.
